pr_title: planner: make index merge union case aware of order property
pr_body:
<!--

2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

Please create an issue first to describe the problem.

There MUST be one line starting with "Issue Number:  " and
linking the relevant issues via the "close" or "ref".

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.

-->

Issue Number: close https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/48359

Problem Summary:

### What changed and how does it work?
As shown in the issue, currently index merge path generation can not feel its parent's property, and this kind of generation contains pruning logic inside ahead, so for this case, since ac and bc index pathes here has the same countAfterAccess as index a and b did, so it will only keep the later one remained.

generation should aware of order property and produce the most suitable index partial pathes combination, which means we should move this generation logic a little bit later when physical enumeration take place, in which parent can ask for what kind of property they want (order by c for this case here)

issue_context.title: planner: the optimizer cannot choose the best IndexMerge plan
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

```
mysql> create table t (a int, b int, c int, key a(a), key b(b), key ac(a, c), key bc(b, c));
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.02 sec)

mysql> explain format='verbose' select * from t where a=1 or b=1 order by c;
+----------------------------------+---------+---------+-----------+---------------------+---------------------------------------------+
| id                               | estRows | estCost | task      | access object       | operator info                               |
+----------------------------------+---------+---------+-----------+---------------------+---------------------------------------------+
| Sort_5                           | 19.99   | 5431.39 | root      |                     | test.t.c                                    |
| └─IndexMerge_14                  | 19.99   | 1019.04 | root      |                     | type: union                                 |
|   ├─IndexRangeScan_11(Build)     | 10.00   | 2035.00 | cop[tikv] | table:t, index:a(a) | range:[1,1], keep order:false, stats:pseudo |
|   ├─IndexRangeScan_12(Build)     | 10.00   | 2035.00 | cop[tikv] | table:t, index:b(b) | range:[1,1], keep order:false, stats:pseudo |
|   └─TableRowIDScan_13(Probe)     | 19.99   | 4881.56 | cop[tikv] | table:t             | keep order:false, stats:pseudo              |
+----------------------------------+---------+---------+-----------+---------------------+---------------------------------------------+
5 rows in set, 1 warning (0.00 sec)

mysql> explain format='verbose' select /*+ use_index_merge(t, ac, bc) */ * from t where a=1 or b=1 order by c;
+----------------------------------+---------+---------+-----------+-------------------------+--------------------------------------------+
| id                               | estRows | estCost | task      | access object           | operator info                              |
+----------------------------------+---------+---------+-----------+-------------------------+--------------------------------------------+
| Projection_17                    | 19.99   | 1225.69 | root      |                         | test.t.a, test.t.b, test.t.c               |
| └─IndexMerge_16                  | 19.99   | 1219.71 | root      |                         | type: union                                |
|   ├─IndexRangeScan_13(Build)     | 10.00   | 2273.08 | cop[tikv] | table:t, index:ac(a, c) | range:[1,1], keep order:true, stats:pseudo |
|   ├─IndexRangeScan_14(Build)     | 10.00   | 2273.08 | cop[tikv] | table:t, index:bc(b, c) | range:[1,1], keep order:true, stats:pseudo |
|   └─TableRowIDScan_15(Probe)     | 19.99   | 4881.56 | cop[tikv] | table:t                 | keep order:false, stats:pseudo             |
+----------------------------------+---------+---------+-----------+-------------------------+--------------------------------------------+
5 rows in set (0.00 sec)
```

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)

It should choose the IndexMerge using `ac + bc`.

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)

It choose the IndexMerge using `a + b`

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->

```
Git Commit Hash: ece2375df4ec70f57168a5e4e2fc4e420d3913e4
```
comments: We mark this issue's affect version starting from 7.1 ince the ORDER PROP's push-down is fully supported from 7.1

review_comments: I'm a bit skeptical about whether we really need to deliberately avoid choosing the same index.

i think if we have a>2 or a<1, we can directly derive a $(-\infty, 1) \cup (2, +\infty)$ on a simple index range scan of a.
rather than index merge $\\{a1:  (-\infty, 1),  a2: (2, +\infty)\\}$ 

old logic, just keep them identical here.
That makes sense. However, if so, do we really need this sorting logic? I can't come up with any real cases that need this logic.

I mean if there are real examples like SQLs?
In such a case, I think, can we just choose a single-index plan on `pk`, or just allow using two partial paths using the same index?

> I mean if there are real examples like SQLs? 
the modification here comes from an old unit test case failure, so I changed the logic like this.

the main reason is that: the user specified an index merge hint, then we pruned other paths in deriveStats there, the only left path is validated for index merge choosing already (not all a simple index, otherwise, index merge hint is inapplicable right?), so the concrete path should successfully be chosen/gen-ed by a kind of order that we want when validating them before.

Looks like `PartialAlternativeIndexPaths` is still missing here.
Or is this deliberate?
Could you add an example for this method?
I'm a bit confused here. Do we allow using the same index for different partial paths here again? Looks like it contradicts the logic above.

this functionality is used in test: TestIndexMergePathGeneration, which has made some assertions with the logical plan after deriveStats, where PartialIndexPaths will be nil according to the design in this pull request
